claims.text: In the space of just three weeks, the UN Human Rights Office documented 15 drone strikes on El Obeid, which killed at least 45 civilians. El Obeid has more than half a million residents, together with at least 100,000 internally displaced persons, and the number of newly displaced people across Kordofan has risen by nearly two-thirds in only three months.

Re-checked 3 August 2026: a search of reliefweb.int and news.un.org found no new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond those already cited; siege and drone-strike conditions continue with no ceasefire or ground assault reported.

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA: renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan state, have put civilians, critical infrastructure and humanitarian operations at risk. UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher said humanitarians are scaling up efforts to reach families hit by conflict in North Kordofan and will seize every opening to expand lifesaving aid in and around El Obeid. OCHA noted that approximately $1.2 billion of the $2.9 billion required for Sudan's 2026 humanitarian response had been received. No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid was published in this update.

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA: 'Renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid ... have also put civilians, critical infrastructure and humanitarian operations at risk.' No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+).

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch of reliefweb.int/country/sdn: no El-Obeid-specific aggregate death toll or IDP figure has been published beyond the 3 July 2026 UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July 2026 WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); the most recent El-Obeid-specific ReliefWeb item remains a 31 July 2026 Plan International piece on cholera risk, with no new casualty/IDP numbers.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: UN News (3 August 2026) reports renewed drone strikes threatening civilians and aid operations in El Obeid but gives no new aggregate death toll or IDP count; ReliefWeb's Sudan country page shows no new El-Obeid-specific casualty/IDP figures beyond what's already cited (45+ deaths, UN Human Rights Office 3 July; 120,000+ IDPs, WFP 17 July).

UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA, reports renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid threatening civilians, infrastructure and humanitarian operations, and cites more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city — a figure of different scope from WFP's 17 July count of 120,000+ in the Unified IDP Camp alone. No new aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (at least 45 civilians killed).

UN News (10 August 2026), citing OCHA: RSF forces have encircled El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, threatening a full-scale ground assault as civilians flock to the city and surrounding areas in search of safety and assistance. Humanitarian partners delivered two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe water shortages. The UN Secretary-General's Personal Envoy has held meetings with both sides and is working toward a full cessation of hostilities. No new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid was published in this update, beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+).

Re-checked 12 August 2026: UN News's most recent Sudan article (10 August 2026, on the RSF encirclement of El Obeid) remains the latest allowlisted report on this event; no article dated after 10 August with new El-Obeid-specific figures was found. No death toll newer than the 3 July UN Human Rights Office figure (at least 45 civilians killed) and no IDP figure newer than WFP's 17 July figure (120,000+ in the Unified IDP Camp alone) has been published.

UN News (12 August 2026), citing OCHA: 'Multiple waves of drone strikes were reported on Wednesday across El Obeid, the North Kordofan capital'... 'roughly 15,000 families have been displaced to El Obeid over the past three weeks,' driven by continuing attacks and insecurity in northern parts of the state, with OCHA noting the influx is 'putting greater pressure on displacement sites and basic services that are already overstretched.' This is a new inflow-displacement figure, distinct in scope from the existing cumulative death toll (45+ killed, UN Human Rights Office, 3 July 2026) and the Unified IDP Camp population figure (120,000+, WFP, 17 July 2026); no new aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid was reported.

Save the Children, via ReliefWeb (14 August 2026): "Nearly 39,000 children fled to the city of El Obeid in North Kordofan, Sudan, over the first six months of the year, escaping violence and attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure that have uprooted families across the state... The new arrivals are now part of more than 605,000 people living in El Obeid town and Sheikan locality... In April 2026, Save the Children-supported health facilities in Sheikan locality treated 426 children for malnutrition, compared with 195 in March, marking a 118% month-on-month increase... individual [water] consumption has now been reduced to approximately 7 litres per person per day, less than half of the general minimum standard of 15 litres recommended by the World Health Organization during crises."

G7 Foreign Ministers' joint statement on El Obeid, Sudan (14 July 2026): condemns ongoing RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and obstruction of humanitarian access, references the precedent of atrocities in El Fasher, and calls for an immediate ceasefire and compliance with the Jeddah Declaration to protect civilians.

UN News (10 August 2026): RSF drone attacks continue on El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, even as the UN and partners have provided two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe water shortages; separately, 18,000 people were displaced from over 20 villages in West Darfur in the preceding week, and 75,000 displaced persons were cut off from care after three health facilities closed in Central Darfur. Sudan-wide, more than 30 million people need assistance, over 9 million are internally displaced, and the US$3 billion humanitarian appeal is only about 40% funded (US$1.2 billion received).

NRC report (posted 7 July 2026) on El Obeid: families are dying from drone strikes and from hunger as the siege continues, with an aid convoy struck the preceding week; essential services and food access are collapsing further as the blockade persists.

UN News (17 July 2026): the UN human rights chief warned that civilians in El Obeid "have been under siege for 18 months" and face continuous drone strikes, with more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city. WFP is providing food assistance to over 100,000 people in those camps, including nutrition support for 17,000 children, but is distributing only a reduced ration that recipients are sharing with other families. Almost 20 million people in Sudan are now classified as acutely food insecure, and more than 14 million people have been uprooted nationwide since the conflict began.

WFP Geneva Palais briefing note (published 17 July 2026): El Obeid city (population approximately 500,000) is hosting displaced people, with more than 120,000 people in the 'Unified IDP Camp' alone. WFP is providing food/cash assistance to just over 100,000 people in camps inside the city, but severe funding shortfalls mean recipients are only receiving 50 percent of the ration they should. Fuel scarcity has crippled partner logistics, forcing WFP to deploy its own fleet vehicles to keep distributions running.

UNFPA Flash Update #2 on the situation in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan (published 20 July 2026, covering 1-19 July): 21 drone-related incidents were recorded in and around El Obeid between 1-19 July 2026, causing civilian casualties (no aggregate death toll given), damage to critical infrastructure, and further disruption to already-limited essential services, with severe constraints on sexual and reproductive health and gender-based-violence response services due to insecurity and resource shortages.

UN News (24 July 2026), citing a UN Women statement: 'More than half a million people live [in El Obeid], including 83,000 internally displaced people, most of them women and children.' Drone strikes have targeted water points and distribution sites during the day, forcing women and girls to wait until nightfall to collect water, where they face sexual violence instead — UN Women describes this as leaving 'no safe window' to access water. Nationwide, 'drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians in the first four months of 2026 alone — more than 80 per cent of all civilian deaths recorded by the human rights office in that period.' The number of women and girls needing gender-based-violence services nationwide has quadrupled since the conflict began, reaching an estimated 12.7 million in 2026, and cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: no allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); siege and drone-strike conditions continue with no de-escalation, ceasefire, or ground assault reported.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: UNHCR's Sudan Situation Monthly External Update #120 (June 2026, posted 31 July 2026) notes continued drone attacks on El Obeid damaging civilian areas, fuel infrastructure, health facilities and transport routes, but reports no new aggregate casualty or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the sources already cited; siege conditions continue with no ceasefire or ground assault confirmed.

description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary forces have besieged El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state, subjecting the city of more than half a million residents to relentless drone strikes and blockade conditions. As of 24 July 2026, the siege continues with no ceasefire and no ground assault yet confirmed by authoritative sources. Drone strikes have intensified (21 incidents recorded 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update on ReliefWeb, up from 15 strikes over three weeks in the prior UN Human Rights Office count) and the humanitarian situation remains dire: WFP reported more than 120,000 people sheltering in the city's Unified IDP Camp alone (17 July briefing), with food rations cut to 50 percent of full entitlement due to funding shortfalls, while a separate UN News/UN Women report (24 July 2026) put El Obeid's IDP population at 83,000 out of a total city population of more than half a million — a lower figure than the WFP camp count, likely reflecting a different counting methodology or reference date, and not treated here as superseding the more specific WFP camp figure. That 24 July report also describes a 'dual terror' facing women and girls, who face drone strikes if they collect water by day and sexual violence if they wait until night, and cites a nationwide (not El Obeid-specific) figure that drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians across Sudan in the first four months of 2026 alone — more than 80 percent of all civilian deaths recorded by the UN human rights office in that period — plus a UN Women estimate that 12.7 million women and girls nationwide now need gender-based-violence services, having quadrupled since the conflict began. No updated aggregate civilian death toll specific to El Obeid has been issued since the UN's 3 July report of at least 45 killed. G7 foreign ministers condemned the siege on 14 July 2026, and UN officials continue to warn of the risk of large-scale atrocities similar to those already documented in El Fasher, Darfur. Re-checked 5 August 2026: UN News (3 August 2026), citing OCHA, reported renewed drone attacks in recent days in El Obeid, with UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher saying humanitarians are scaling up efforts to reach families in North Kordofan; no new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the figures already cited. Re-checked 8 August 2026: UN News (3 August 2026) reports renewed drone strikes threatening civilians and aid operations in El Obeid but gives no new aggregate death toll or IDP count; ReliefWeb's Sudan country page shows no new El-Obeid-specific casualty/IDP figures beyond what's already cited (45+ deaths, UN Human Rights Office 3 July; 120,000+ IDPs, WFP 17 July). Re-checked 9 August 2026: UN News (3 August 2026) reports renewed drone attacks on El Obeid in recent days and cites more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in the city's camps — a figure with different scope from WFP's 17 July count of 120,000+ in the Unified IDP Camp alone, so it is not adopted as a headline revision. No allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed). Re-checked 11 August 2026: UN News (10 August 2026), citing OCHA, reports that RSF forces have now encircled El Obeid and are threatening a full-scale ground assault as civilians flock to the city and surrounding areas seeking safety; humanitarian partners delivered two million litres of drinking water to about 133,000 people amid severe water shortages, and the UN Secretary-General's Personal Envoy has met both sides while working toward a full cessation of hostilities. This marks an escalation from prior updates (which had found no confirmed ground assault), though no new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid has been published beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); a separate 2 August drone strike on a traditional court in Garra al-Zawaya, North Darfur (reported to have killed at least 35 people) occurred in a different location and is not counted toward the El Obeid city toll. Re-checked 12 August 2026: UN News's 10 August 2026 report on the RSF encirclement of El Obeid remains the latest allowlisted update; no aggregate death toll or IDP figure newer than the 3 July (45+ killed) and 17 July (120,000+ IDPs) figures already on file has been published. If anything the situation is escalating, not resolving: no ceasefire or lifting of the encirclement has been confirmed. UN News (12 August 2026, citing OCHA) reports multiple waves of drone strikes across El Obeid and roughly 15,000 families newly displaced into the city over the prior three weeks, straining already-overstretched displacement sites and services; this is additional inflow context and does not supersede the existing death toll or camp population figures, which use different scopes. Re-checked 14 August 2026: a new Save the Children report via ReliefWeb (14 August 2026) reports nearly 39,000 children have arrived in El Obeid as displaced persons over the past six months, and that the city (with Sheikan locality) now hosts more than 605,000 people total — a broader population figure than the previously-cited 500,000+ resident count — plus new malnutrition and water-scarcity data (individual water consumption down to ~7 litres/person/day). This does not supersede the existing 45+ deaths (3 July) or 120,000+ IDP camp figure (17 July), which use different scope/metrics, but confirms the siege situation continues to deteriorate with no ceasefire. Re-checked 15 August 2026: no allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the 3 July 2026 UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); a non-allowlisted Xinhua report (15 August 2026) of at least 14 killed in an attack near El Obeid is not corroborated on ohchr.org, reliefweb.int, or wfp.org and is not incorporated. Re-checked 16 August 2026: UN News (10 August) reports RSF drone attacks continuing on El Obeid even as humanitarian agencies scale up water assistance (2 million litres to ~133,000 people) under serious security constraints; nationally, Sudan's humanitarian caseload remains catastrophic (30M+ in need, 9M+ IDPs) against a badly underfunded ($1.2B of $3B) response, with no indication of the siege lifting. Re-checked 17 August 2026: no allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the 3 July 2026 UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); UN News's most recent Sudan article (12 August 2026, on renewed attacks and displacement in Blue Nile and North Kordofan) remains the latest allowlisted update, with no ceasefire or lifting of the RSF encirclement confirmed. Re-checked 18 August 2026: UN News's most recent Sudan/El Obeid article remains the 12 August 2026 report on renewed drone strikes and displacement into El Obeid (already on file, news.un.org/en/story/2026/08/1168126); no article dated after 12 August was found via search, and a direct re-fetch of that article confirms it gives no updated aggregate death toll or IDP figure for El Obeid beyond those already cited (45+ killed, UN Human Rights Office, 3 July; 120,000+ IDPs in the Unified IDP Camp, WFP, 17 July). A search of ReliefWeb found nothing newer than the 14 August Save the Children report already cited. A non-allowlisted Xinhua report of at least 14 killed near El Obeid (Um Arada, 14-15 August) remains uncorroborated on ohchr.org, reliefweb.int or wfp.org and is not incorporated. No ceasefire or lifting of the RSF encirclement has been confirmed.

impact.summary: No updated aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid has been published since the 3 July UN Human Rights Office figure (15 drone strikes over 3 weeks, at least 45 civilians killed); drone strikes have continued and even increased in frequency (21 drone-related incidents logged 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update via ReliefWeb), but no authoritative source has issued a new cumulative city-specific casualty count as of 24 July 2026. Rations for WFP-assisted families remain cut to 50 percent of the full entitlement due to funding shortfalls. The 24 July report also documents that women and girls face drone strikes if they collect water by day and sexual violence if they wait until after dark, with no safe window to access water. No ceasefire, siege-lifting, or ground assault has been confirmed by an authoritative source.
